what_it_does: Large web applications are built from dozens of small, independently running services (microservices) that call each other in a chain. When too many services run on the same server simultaneously, they compete for CPU and memory, slowing down the whole application. Existing auto-scaling tools — software that automatically spins up more copies of a service under load — focus only on the slowest service in the chain and ignore the others, missing efficiency gains. Grad learns a performance model for each microservice individually, then uses mathematical gradient information (rate of change in latency as resources change) to decide which services — including non-bottleneck ones — are worth scaling at any given moment. A fast end-to-end latency predictor lets Grad simulate the effect of scaling decisions in real time before committing to them.
